[MUJAHID:v1p304/r1] MUJAHID, d. 104 · مجاهد | holds | The words about sailing and mooring in God's name mean invoking God when boarding, sailing, and coming to rest.
[MUJAHID:v1p304/r2] MUJAHID, d. 104 · مجاهد | holds | The water's subsiding means that it decreased.
[MUQATIL:11:41-43/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Noah tells the passengers to say God's name when the ark starts and stops; God is forgiving and merciful for saving them from punishment.
[MAJAZ:v1p289/r1] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | Majrāhā means its course or journey, from “it ran with them”; another reading takes it from ajraytuhā, “I made it run.”
[MAJAZ:v1p289/r2] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | reports | Labīd’s verse uses mujra Dāḥis for the race or course of Dāḥis; ḥarsan means a long duration.
[MAJAZ:v1p289/r3] MAJAZ, d. 209 · author | holds | Mursāhā means its stopping place, the verbal noun of arsāytuhā, “I moored it.”
[AKHFASH:v1p382/r3] AKHFASH, d. 215 · author | holds | مجرىها and مرساها can derive from the form أجريت and أرسيت.
[AKHFASH:v1p382/r4] AKHFASH, d. 215 · بعضهم | reports | Some derive مجراها and مرساها from the basic verbs جريت and رست.
[AKHFASH:v1p382/r5] AKHFASH, d. 215 · بعضهم | reports | Some read مجريها ومرسيها as descriptions of God, making Him the one who causes it to sail and moor.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#2/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | Majrāhā means the ship's course or journey.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p204#2/r2] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | Marsāhā means where it is moored or comes to rest; the related verb can also mean to stop.
[TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The account omits that Noah carried the people aboard; the previous command to load and the following “board” make that action understood.
[TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قراء أهل المدينة والبصرة وبعض الكوفيين | reports | Most Medinan, Basran, and some Kufan readers pronounce both forms with ḍamma as verbal nouns from causative forms; each can be nominative as “its running and anchoring” or accusative as “at its running and anchoring.” | mentions 1:1
[TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قراء الكوفيين | reports | Most Kufan readers open the mīm of majrāhā and damma the mīm of marsāhā, deriving them from jarā and arsā; the same two syntactic parses apply.
[TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · أبو رجاء العطاردي | reports | Abū Rajāʾ reads both as active participles describing God as the one who makes the ark run and anchors it; genitive is likelier, though accusative as a circumstantial is possible.
[TAB-FULL:v12p413#2/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · بعض الكوفيين | reports | Some Kufans open both mīms, treating the words as the ark’s states of sailing and anchoring; al-Ṭabarī cites ʿAntarah’s use of tarsū as poetic evidence.
[TAB-FULL:v12p416/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | prefers | Al-Ṭabarī chooses fatḥa in majrāhā and ḍamma in marsāhā: the former matches the nearby “it sails” in 11:42, while the latter follows the reciters’ consensus. | mentions 11:42
[TAB-FULL:v12p416/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Majrāhā means the ark’s passage, and marsāhā its stopping, which God causes.
[TAB-FULL:v12p416/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid reads both mīms with ḍamma.
[TAB-FULL:v12p416/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid explains the invocation as said when they board, sail, and dock.
[TAB-FULL:v12p416/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says invoking God’s name makes the ark sail or anchor whenever Noah intends either action.
[TAB-FULL:v12p416/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | God is forgiving to those who repent and return to Him, and merciful not to punish them after repentance.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r10] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The forms may also be understood as the verbal nouns from jarat tajrī and rasat tarsū; al-marsā is its place of rest.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r11] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The command is to invoke God's name when the ship is sailing and when it settles; marsāhā is in the genitive as an attribute of God.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r12] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | rejects | The unrecited form mujrihā should not be read because recitation is transmitted practice, though it admits a circumstantial parse meaning one who runs and moors it.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r13] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | On that unrecited form, mujrihā may be an accusative of praise.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r14] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Alternatively, mujrihā and mursīhā may be nominative with an omitted huwa.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r6] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | By God's name means that the ship runs through God and settles through Him.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r7] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Readings include majrāhā with open mīm and marsāhā with ḍamma, both with ḍamma, and other forms; all are correct and good.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r8] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | With open mīm, majrāhā means its running and marsāhā its mooring: by God it is brought to rest.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p51/r9] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | With both mīms in ḍamma, the phrase means that God causes it to run and to moor; ajraytuhu and ijrāʾ are synonymous.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · قتادة | reports | Noah boarded during the first ten days of Rajab and left the ark during the first ten days of Muharram, fasting with his family from dusk to dusk.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r2] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · أبو صالح | reports | Abu Salih says Noah boarded with his three sons, wife, and the sons' three wives, totaling eight; the sons were Japheth, Ham, and Sam.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r3] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · أبو صالح | reports | He says Ham had intercourse with his wife aboard, so Noah prayed for his offspring's complexion to change, and the Sudanese resulted.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r4] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | Another report gives eighty men with their families and a 150-day voyage.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r5] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | The ark was directed to Mecca, circled the Kaaba for forty days, then was directed to Mount Judi and settled there.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r6] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | Noah first sent a raven, which landed on carrion and delayed; a dove returned with an olive leaf and mud on its feet, showing the water had receded.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r7] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · ابن عباس | reports | Noah built a village at the foot of Judi called Eighty; its inhabitants' tongues divided into eighty languages, including Arabic, and Noah interpreted among them.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r8] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · جابر بن زيد | reports | He calls Allah the Greatest Name, arguing that it begins before every other name throughout the Qur'an.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2032/r9] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · الضحاك | reports | He assigns the basmala's letters to God's splendor, glory, and sovereignty, and says Allah is the deity of creation.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · الشعبي | reports | He reports that the Prophet wrote four documents, the first beginning 'In Your name, O God'; then Hud's surah was revealed with 'In God's name is its sailing and mooring.'
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r2] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · الضحاك | reports | Noah said 'In God's name is its sailing' when he wanted the ark to move and 'its mooring' when he wanted it to stop.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r3] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · مجاهد | reports | He glosses 'In God's name' as said when boarding, with the remaining words referring to sailing and mooring.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r4] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | He advises passengers to recall God's favor and recite Noah's words when boarding; on an animal, one should mention God's name.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r5] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | He says Satan urges a person who rides without invoking God to sing, and if he does not sing, to walk.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r6] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · رزين بن حبيش | reports | He says the ark moored at the site by Kufa's Kinda gate, explaining why he prayed there on Fridays.
[IBNABIHATIM:v6p2033/r7] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · سعيد بن جبير | reports | He explains 'forgiving, merciful' as forgiveness for their former idolatry and mercy after their repentance.
[NAHHAS:v2p282/r10] NAHHAS, d. 338 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid, Muslim ibn Jundub, and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read mujrihā and mursīhā.
[NAHHAS:v2p282/r11] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The first reading means by God's name its running and anchoring; marsāhā is nominative as a subject or may be accusative meaning at the time it runs.
[NAHHAS:v2p282/r12] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | reports | Another parse supplies mawḍiʿ, meaning in God's name is the place of its movement, then omits mawḍiʿ and uses majrāhā in its place.
[NAHHAS:v2p282/r13] NAHHAS, d. 338 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says that when Noah said in God's name, the ark moved, and when he said in God's name, it came to rest.
[NAHHAS:v2p282/r14] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The bāʾ attaches to irkabū; the open-mīm forms derive from running and settling, while mujrihā and mursīhā may be God's genitive adjectives, an implied nominative, or accusatives of state.
[NAHHAS:v2p282/r8] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | reports | The two mīms are ḍamma in the reading of the two sanctuaries and Basrans except a few; al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī open the mīm of majrāhā and round that of marsāhā.
[NAHHAS:v2p282/r9] NAHHAS, d. 338 · يحيى بن وثاب | reports | A report through Yaḥyā ibn ʿĪsā gives Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb's reading with both mīms open.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v4p329/r1] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر | reports | These readers pronounce the mīm of majrāhā with ḍamma.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v4p329/r2] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم | reports | These readers pronounce the mīm with fatḥa and the rāʾ with kasra; the source notes this is the Qurʾan’s only rāʾ with kasra.

[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p473/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says Noah boarded the ark on 10 Rajab and left it on 10 Muharram, Ashura; he told those fasting to complete the fast and the others to fast that day.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p473/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | Mujrayaha means setting the vessel in motion and mursaha means bringing it to rest; Noah said God's name when starting and stopping it.
[QUSHAYRI:v2p44/r9] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Noah's safety in the flood came through God's name, reliance upon Him, and His favor, not through multiplying schemes.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Noah tells those he ordered to board to ride; rakiba broadly means to mount or rise onto something, including an animal, ship, land, or sea, and also occurs in the expression for debt burdening someone.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Arabs call passengers on a ship rukāb al-safīna, whereas rukbān, arkūb, and rukb refer to riders of animals and camels.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن أحمر | reports | Ibn Aḥmar calls ship passengers rukbānan in a poem, supporting the broader usage for seafarers.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Fī cannot depend on the verb rukūb because Arabic says “I rode the ship,” not “I rode in the ship”; the object is omitted, understood as water, and fīhā is circumstantial.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p420/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Alternatively, the meaning is “board it,” with fī as an emphatic addition; it directs them to the ark’s interior, since simply saying “board it” might suggest its deck. | mentions 12:43

[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Marsā is a verbal noun from arsā, to become fixed or to make something fixed; 79:32 says God fixed the mountains. | mentions 79:32
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس في رواية عطاء | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ, says the ship runs by God’s name and power.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Noah said “In God’s name” when he wanted the ship to sail, and again when he wanted it to settle.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو إسحاق | reports | Abū Isḥāq says the ship sails by God and settles by Him; bismillāh here means “by God,” so the reported explanations share one meaning.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r7] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء | reports | Al-Farrāʾ offers two parses: majrāhā and marsāhā may be raised by the preposition bi, or bismillāh can stand alone while both nouns are accusative as adverbials of running and settling.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p421/r8] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن الأنباري | reports | Ibn al-Anbārī explains the first parse: bi is grammatically the predicate and raises the subject, while its sense is accusative, “its running occurs by God’s name.”
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الفراء، ابن الأنباري | reports | The second of al-Farrāʾ and Ibn al-Anbārī’s parses makes majrāhā accusative as a time or place expression: “in its running and settling,” with the preposition omitted.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أحمد بن يحيى | reports | Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā supplies an omitted verb for bi; it governs majrāhā, as in “its running and settling take place by God’s name.”
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو علي الفارسي | reports | Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī reads bismillāh as a circumstantial phrase for the riders, who board blessed by God’s name; compare the expression at 5:61. | mentions 5:61
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو علي الفارسي | reports | On his reading, majrāhā and marsāhā are temporal adverbials for the two inevitable periods of sailing and mooring, not times when they are commanded to board.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p422/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Abū ʿAlī’s circumstantial parse is a separate interpretation from the explanations attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p424/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says God is forgiving toward the people in the ark and merciful to them.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p424/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أهل المعاني | reports | The mention of forgiveness and mercy coheres with rescue by boarding: those blessings are obtained through obedience just as rescue was obtained.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:41-43/r1] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Noah told those aboard to board the ark, invoking God's name for sailing and landing; saying the name made the ship move or stop.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:41-43/r2] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Noah described God as forgiving and merciful to those aboard.
[DAMGHANI:v1p209/r2] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Riding here means boarding or being aboard a ship; the cited Noah passage parallels other ship-riding verses. | mentions 36:42, 29:65
[JISHUMI:v5p3499/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · حمزة والكسائي وحفص | reports | They read مجراها with fatḥa on mīm; the others read with ḍamma.
[JISHUMI:v5p3499/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · محمد بن محيصن | reports | All readers except Muḥammad ibn Muḥayṣin use ḍamma in مرساها; he opens both mīms and treats both words as verbal nouns meaning the Ark's running and anchoring by God.
[JISHUMI:v5p3499/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | With ḍamma, the words mean God causes the Ark to run and anchor, like Qur'anic verbal-noun forms for lodging, entering, and exiting; matching the two vowels is preferred.
[JISHUMI:v5p3499/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · حفص عن عاصم | reports | Ḥafṣ reads يابني with fatḥa on yāʾ throughout the Qur'an; the other readers use kasra, except for Ibn Kathīr's differing report in Luqmān.
[JISHUMI:v5p3499/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The kasra reading transfers the vowel of the deleted hamzat al-waṣl to yāʾ; fatḥa is lighter, while yāʾ and kasra together are considered heavy.
[JISHUMI:v5p3499/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Jary means rapid movement and can name an agent or trustee because he acts in place of his principal.
[JISHUMI:v5p3499/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Irsa is securing a ship so that it stops; related usages describe something fixed or standing firm, including mountains and cooking pots.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p178/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · حمزة والكسائي وحفص | reports | Hamza, al-Kisai, and Hafs read مجريها with an opened meem and its verbal sense of running, while the accompanying مَرساها has a damma.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · أبي | reports | Ubayy's codex reads “ʿalā ismi Allāh” in place of “bi-smi Allāh.”
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | One parsing makes bi-smi Allāh a circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in “board”: board seeking God's blessing; majrāhā and mursāhā are temporal adverbs for sailing and mooring, governed by the verbal sense of the basmala.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | Another parsing makes bi-smi Allāh the predicate and majrāhā/mursāhā verbal nouns as subject: the ship's sailing and mooring occur by God's blessing; the sentence is circumstantial with the pronoun in “therein.”
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The second parsing cannot be a circumstantial clause attached to the command “board,” because it contains no pronoun referring back to that command.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Dahhak says Noah said the basmala whenever he wanted the ship to move or stop, and it responded accordingly.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر | reports | Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim in Abu Bakr's transmission, and Ibn ʿAmir read both forms with ḍamma on the mīm, as verbal nouns for sailing and mooring; many other authorities also read this way, and Labid supplies poetic evidence.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم | reports | Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from ʿAsim read majrāhā with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the rāʾ, while retaining ḍamma in mursāhā.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p172#2/r9] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الأعمش وابن مسعود | reports | Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Masʿud read both words with fatḥa on their mīms, treating them as places of running and settling.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الطبري | prefers | Al-Tabari chooses the reading of majrāhā with fatḥa on the first mīm and ḍamma on the second, arguing from “it sails”; Ibn Masʿud also read the phrase, transmitted by Abu Waʾil and Masruq.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن وثاب وأبو رجاء العطاري والنخعي والجحدري والكلبي والضحاك بن مزاحم ومسلم بن جندب وأهل الشام | reports | These readers say mujrihā and mursīhā, two active-participle attributes of God, referring back to God in “in the name of God.”
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p173/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The statement “my Lord is forgiving, merciful” reminds the believers of God's blessings, mercy, concealment, and forgiveness of their sins upon their repentance and return to Him.
[TABRISI:11:40-42/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر | reports | The Kūfan readers except Abū Bakr read majrāhā with fatḥa on the mīm; the others use ḍamma.
[TABRISI:11:40-42/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · ابن محيصن | reports | All agree on ḍamma in mursal, apart from an anomalous report from Ibn Muḥayṣin opening the mīm in both words.
[TABRISI:11:40-43#2/r13] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The passengers are told to board the ark, with omitted narrative understood: after the flood began and Noah recognized God's sign of the unbelievers' destruction, he called his family and followers aboard.
[TABRISI:11:40-43#2/r14] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | They invoke God's name for blessing at the ark's setting out and anchoring.
[TABRISI:11:40-43/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | The explanation of the reading فتح مجريها appeals to the following phrase وهي تجري بهم; the kasra reading is supported by the equivalent senses of جرت بهم and أجرتهم.
[TABRISI:11:40-43/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The verbs جرى and أجرى are close in meaning, whether one says a thing sailed, made it sail, or sailed with it.
[TABRISI:11:41/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو علي | reports | Abū ʿAlī says bismi Allāh majrāhā can be a circumstantial phrase attached either to the pronoun in ride or to the pronoun in it, depending on the syntax.
[TABRISI:11:41/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو علي | reports | If bismi Allāh is a fronted predicate or majrāhā is raised by the adverb, the phrase can only describe the pronoun in it, since it has no reference back to the pronoun in ride.
[TABRISI:11:41/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو علي | reports | Under another parse, bismi Allāh describes those commanded to ride, as in riding equipped with weapons or clothed; they ride invoking and relying on God.
[TABRISI:11:41/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو علي | reports | On that parse, majrāhā attaches to the verbal sense of bismi Allāh and marks the times of running and anchoring; it does not modify ride, since they are not told to board at those times.
[TABRISI:11:41/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · أبو علي | holds | Majrāhā is accusative as an adverb in the latter analysis, and nominative through an initial subject or adverb in the first.
[TABRISI:11:43#2/r1] TABRISI, d. 548 · الضحاك | reports | Al-Dahhak says they said God's name when they wanted the ark to sail, and again when they wanted it to stop.
[TABRISI:11:43#2/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Mentioning God as forgiving and merciful follows the account of rescue by boarding: mercy is sought through obedience just as rescue came through boarding.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r1] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | holds | Rukūb means mounting or being atop something; rikāb usually means riding animals.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r2] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · ابن فارس | reports | Ibn Fāris says related rider terms apply only to camels; al-Khalīl also uses rikāb for a ship's equipment.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p311/r3] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | Rukūb can mean riding beasts and ships. | mentions 16:8
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Noah addressed those he had been ordered to carry and told them to board the ark.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r10] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو رزين، أبو المتوكل | reports | They read majrāhā with fatḥa on mīm and rāʾ, and marsāhā with raised mīm and fatḥa sīn.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r11] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو الجوزاء، ابن يعمر | reports | They read both words with fatḥa on mīm and on rāʾ or sīn.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r12] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · يحيى بن وثاب | reports | He opens both mīms but applies imāla to both rāʾ and sīn.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r13] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو عمران الجوني، ابن جبير | reports | They raise both mīms and open rāʾ and sīn, followed by alif.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r14] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | With ḍamma mīm the forms derive from أجرى and أرسى; with fatḥa mīm they are verbal nouns from jarā and rasā.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r15] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الزجاج | reports | By God’s name means by God; Noah told them to name God when the ark moved and when it came to rest.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | One report says they boarded on 10 Rajab and left the ark on ʿĀshūrāʾ.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن جريج | reports | The ark rose from ʿAyn Warda on Friday, 10 Rajab, circled the site of the raised Kaʿba seven times, and landed at Baqardā on al-Jūdī on ʿĀshūrāʾ.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | When a mouse gnawed the ark’s ropes, God inspired Noah to rub a lion’s tail, producing two cats.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | A further story says Noah complained about the filth; after God’s instruction he rubbed the elephant’s tail, and two pigs emerged and ate it.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Readers differ on the vowels of majrāhā and marsāhā: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bakr read majrāhā with ḍamma on mīm; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read it with fatḥa mīm and kasra rāʾ.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | All read marsāhā with ḍamma mīm; Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ open sīn, while Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr use an intermediate pronunciation and Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf incline it.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r8] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الحسن، قتادة، حميد الأعرج، إسماعيل بن مجالد عن عاصم | reports | These authorities alone make the two participles divine attributes, reading mujrihā and mursihā with ḍamma mīm and two yāʾs.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p107#2/r9] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن مسعود | reports | Ibn Masʿūd reads majrāhā with fatḥa mīm and imāla on rāʾ, and marsāhā with raised mīm and imāla on sīn.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Readers vocalizing both mims with ḍamma understand the ship's running and anchoring as by God; readers with fatḥa understand God as the agent of their occurrence.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p109/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو منصور اللغوي | reports | Abu Mansur distinguishes the readings as causative, “God made it run,” versus intransitive, “it ran.”
